text: Cell-free protein synthesis reactions are self-replicating, meaning a single reaction mixture can be propagated indefinitely without adding fresh extract or purified components.
explanation: This is false: the chapter explicitly lists 'not self-replicating' as a disadvantage of cell-free systems, since each new reaction must be reconstituted from extract or purified parts rather than growing and dividing on its own. This lack of self-replication is precisely why cell-free systems are limited to hour-scale reactions rather than ongoing fermentation.
